tasks.title: Characterize legacy projection ownership lanes
tasks.goal: Freeze existing per-operation behavior before replacing the fixed client catalog.
steps: Enumerate existing standalone skill, automatic binding and lifecycle deploy operations by client, scope and file/tree/config shape.
Build isolated fixtures capturing exact paths, bytes, supported operations and receipt owner; distinguish coarse MCP scope flags from project skill support.
Record compatibility cases for logical config members versus physical locks and equal-byte foreign occupants.
positive_cases: Existing supported install/update/remove shapes retain their exact bytes and ownership.
Codex project skill behavior is characterized separately from user-only MCP config.
negative_cases: A second receipt family cannot silently claim an equal-byte occupant.
Unsupported directory/resource shape is an explicit case, not omitted coverage.
acceptance: A per-surface matrix links each row to an executable characterization case.
Fixtures use injected homes and preserve unrelated configuration.
tasks.safe_stop: Legacy characterization passes before replacing client data structures.
tasks.commit_subject: test(adapters): characterize legacy scopes and receipt ownership
notes: fixtures/next/adapters is a proposed fixture subtree. Do not treat current coarse booleans as the future capability contract.
Registration perimeter includes existing crate manifests and module owners only for required exports/dependencies; do not change unrelated declarations.

tasks.title: Specify four client contracts from exact versions
tasks.goal: Define the required Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Qwen Code contracts without implying untested support.
steps: For each mandatory client bind an exact available version and official resource/config/launch documentation; record platform and source of observation.
Translate required skills, MCP/config and plugin surfaces into operation/scope/shape rows with explicit target paths and value grammar.
Define positive commissioning cases and unsupported-version refusals; keep Gemini/Copilot secondary and existing legacy clients intact.
positive_cases: All four mandatory clients have exact versioned requested surfaces and acceptance cases.
A missing executable/version remains explicit evidence debt.
negative_cases: Presence markers or official docs alone cannot count as runtime support.
Qwen must not be represented only by adding a fourth hardcoded executable field.
acceptance: The matrix distinguishes observed facts, proposed adapter data and unexecuted gates.
Every mandatory lifecycle scenario has a concrete future isolated proof.
tasks.safe_stop: Four-client contracts are reviewable; no real user settings or client installation changed.
tasks.commit_subject: docs(adapters): define exact four-client commissioning contracts
notes: Read-only official-document/probe work at execution time must use explicit preparation. This task never installs into the real home.
Registration perimeter includes existing crate manifests and module owners only for required exports/dependencies; do not change unrelated declarations.
